item.text:
**3B.2 Research Note: Vladimir Putin in 2024**

Bottom line: the 2024 record is **strongly against**. I found one weak pro-side procedural decree, but the dominant evidence shows systematic tolerance of abuse, political imprisonment, torture, and harsh custodial treatment by state organs.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Slightly for 3B.2, but indirect | `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 01.03.2024 г. № 162` | Kremlin | 2024-03-01 | https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/50378/print | Putin amended military statutes to require commanders to prevent crimes and incidents, report problems promptly, and respond to weapons-storage alarms. This is the only 2024 item that weakly points toward discipline and oversight, but it is broad military governance rather than an actual anti-abuse action. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.2 | `Russia: Prisoner of conscience Aleksei Navalny, Kremlin’s most vocal opponent, dies in custody` | Amnesty International | 2024-02-16 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/02/russia-prisoner-of-conscience-aleksei-navalny-kremlins-most-vocal-opponent-dies-in-custody/ | Amnesty says Navalny had been poisoned, unjustly imprisoned, and tortured in prison before dying in custody. This is powerful evidence that the Kremlin tolerated lethal abuse of its most prominent political prisoner. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.2 | `Russia: Authorities punishing imprisoned anti-war critics and dissenters by denying family contact` | Amnesty International | 2024-06-26 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/russia-authorities-punishing-imprisoned-anti-war-critics-and-dissenters-by-denying-family-contact/ | Amnesty says Russian authorities systematically denied family contact to arbitrarily imprisoned critics, using legal loopholes and fabricated pretexts. That indicates deliberate tolerance of punitive mistreatment in the prison system. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.2 | `Russian Federation: Further Information: Prosecution of Imprisoned Ukrainian Continues: Oleksandr Marchenko` | Amnesty International | 2024-02-16 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/eur46/7725/2024/en/ | Amnesty reports that Marchenko was harassed and ill-treated in custody, repeatedly placed in punishment cells on spurious grounds, and denied urgent health care. This is direct evidence of tolerated custodial abuse. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.2 | `Russia: Freedom in the World 2024 Country Report` | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says the Kremlin intensified restrictions, used fabricated criminal cases, and that detainees were frequently abused during or after arrest. This points to systemic tolerance of abuse by police and prison authorities. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| Against 3B.2 | `Russia: Nations in Transit 2024 Country Report` | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/russia/nations-transit/2024 | Freedom House reports political persecution, harsh prison conditions, and abuse in pretrial detention centers. It also notes a large antiwar prosecution wave, indicating abuse was embedded in the system rather than restrained. | 3B.2, 3B.1 |

**Synthesis**

- Best-supported answer: **No**. Putin did not prevent abuse by police, prisons, intelligence, or other coercive actors in 2024.
- The strongest evidence is **systemic**: torture, punitive isolation of dissidents, fabricated charges, and death in custody.
- The only pro-side item is a **general discipline decree**, which does not show meaningful anti-abuse enforcement.
- Search gap: I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence of Putin punishing abusive security officials in a way that changed the broader pattern, or of consistent restraint toward political prisoners and detainees.
